query: How can support teams reduce ticket resolution time?

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: A strong grouping axis; teams can compare resolution_minutes across categories. Sample categorisations (billing, auth, outage, feature request, bug) are all sound readings of the source text.

per_column.name: operational_severity
per_column.rationale: Severity is a meaningful driver of resolution time and distinct from priority. Values track the text well (service_down for 502 outage, single_user for one user's issues).

per_column.name: technical_complexity
per_column.rationale: A 1-5 complexity scale is a genuine axis to model resolution time. Groundedness is somewhat softer since exact numeric levels are inferred, but the assignments are plausible readings of the descriptions.

per_column.name: affected_scope
per_column.rationale: Blast radius is useful and partly correlated with severity but adds a distinct dimension. Values are well grounded (entire_tenant for Acme outage, single_user for individual reports).

per_column.name: requires_escalation
per_column.rationale: Escalation need is highly relevant to resolution time. Some values are inferred rather than stated (e.g. engineering_escalation for the SSO session-drop ticket where the customer only wants confirmation), a slightly confident inference, but generally reasonable.

per_column.name: root_cause_domain
per_column.rationale: Root-cause domain gives a useful axis to route/analyse. Some assignments are speculative (auth session drop labeled auth_or_identity is fine; classifying complex cases risks over-confidence), but samples are defensible readings.

per_column.name: customer_urgency_signal
per_column.rationale: Urgency signals plausibly affect prioritisation and resolution speed. Values well grounded: explicit_deadline (Friday book close), active_business_event (board presentation), no_urgency_stated where silent.

per_column.name: workaround_available
per_column.rationale: Presence of a workaround plausibly relates to resolution urgency/time. Values reasonable (workaround_exists for the sed step, not_applicable for feature request), though many rows default to no_workaround which may be over-asserted when text is silent.

per_column.name: data_or_billing_sensitivity
per_column.rationale: Sensitivity flag is useful for identifying tickets needing careful handling. Dominated by not_present (200), reducing leverage somewhat, but values are well grounded (billing_discrepancy for the duplicate line item).

judge.rationale: The added columns provide multiple genuine, distinct axes (category, severity, scope, complexity, urgency, escalation, root cause) that let an analyst group and model resolution_minutes to answer how to reduce resolution time. There is mild redundancy between severity/scope and between category/root_cause, but each still contributes a separable dimension. Groundedness is generally strong: sampled values are sound readings of the source text, with silent rows correctly defaulting to not_present/no_urgency_stated. The softest spots are inferred numeric complexity and some confidently assigned escalation/root-cause labels, but no clear contradictions or invented facts were observed.
